intended_object: An auxiliary cocone. Take a filtered diagram N of sheafed spaces (with sheaves of types) and the limit sheafed space built from a chosen limit cone of the underlying spaces. The cocone sends each stage's global sections to the limit's global sections by pulling back along the limit projections. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The module proves that the colimit of the stages' global sections maps isomorphically to the global sections of the limit sheafed space. This definition only packages the comparison maps Γ(π_i) as a cocone over N.rightOp ⋙ Γ, so that the colimit's universal property gives the map whose bijectivity is then proved. It is a specific cocone fixed to a chosen construction (`limitConeOfSpaceCone`), not a standard mathematical notion with its own place in the literature. The construction itself is correct: the cocone point is Γ of the limit, each leg is Γ applied to a limit projection, and naturality follows from the cone condition. Still, it is a technical device for the proof, so it has no textbook counterpart to compare against.
